editorial_review_row.author: NAFT Editorial
editorial_review_row.content: Grand Capital is a legit operating entity that has survived nearly 20 years in the forex industry without ever obtaining a licence from any recognised financial regulator. Registered in St. Vincent and the Grenadines — a jurisdiction that explicitly does not regulate forex — and operating with zero oversight from FCA, ASIC, CySEC, BaFin, or any equivalent authority in 2026. The FinaCom membership provides a voluntary dispute resolution mechanism but carries no enforcement power and does not constitute regulation by any definition. The Seychelles FSA has issued a public warning against Grand Capital, meaning at least one jurisdiction has formally flagged the entity as non-compliant. Longevity is the sole meaningful trust signal here: brokers that intend to steal deposits outright rarely survive two decades. But survival is not the same as safety. There is no segregated fund requirement enforced by law, no compensation scheme, no negative balance protection mandate, and no regulatory body monitoring Grand Capital's operations in 2026. For traders in the CIS region, Southeast Asia, and Africa where Grand Capital focuses its marketing, regulated alternatives like XM and Exness exist at the same price point with actual oversight. The only scenario where Grand Capital makes sense is if you are an experienced trader who has exhausted all regulated alternatives for your specific jurisdiction — and even then, never deposit more than you can afford to lose entirely.
